A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social and behavioural sciences provide a rich and growing source of evidence for effective response to pandemics.
the social and behavioural science insights are important to help guide the public health response, and there are many gaps in the research literature that should be filled as quickly as possible.

the social and behavioural science community should be working with epidemiologists and public policy experts to identify the most effective strategies to help people navigate the pandemic, to communicate effectively with the public and with policy makers, to understand how to motivate people to change their behaviour, and to identify and support the most vulnerable members of society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social and behavioural science literatures can help inform effective policy responses to COVID 19 and other pandemics, but that the field is still in its infancy and has much more work to do.
social and behavioural science has important lessons for the COVID 19 response.
the social and behavioural science community can and must contribute to this crisis, and that there is a pressing need to do so quickly and in close coordination with other disciplines.
